headline: Ukrainian Repair Festival Moves Underground to Defy War
meta_description: In Chornomorsk, Ukraine, a repair festival relocates to an underground shelter ahead of International Repair Day, turning survival into solidarity.
summary_short: Facing Russian missile strikes, residents of Chornomorsk are holding their repair festival underground on October 17, proving that community resilience thrives even in w…
body:
When a bomb destroyed the college building where Chornomorsk's repair café operated, organisers faced a choice: abandon their plans or adapt. They chose to move their Chornomorsk Repair Festival underground. On October 17, International Repair Day, residents will gather in a shelter beneath their Black Sea city to learn how to fix broken bikes, electronics and clothing—a defiant act of normalcy and community care amid ongoing Russian strikes. For Nataliia Pasenko, an organiser, the decision reflects something deeper than logistics. "We do not want the war to completely take away young people's opportunities to learn, create, experiment, meet one another and imagine their future," she said. "That is why holding it, even under these circumstances, matters so much to us."

The festival embodies a powerful paradox: while discussing repair and restoration, Ukrainians are simultaneously learning to repair and restore the everyday life around them. Visitors will explore a 'Take Me Apart' experimental zone where they can discover how ordinary objects work—a chance to build skills and understanding in a moment when both feel precious. Pasenko emphasises that this simple act carries profound weight right now. "When we fix something broken, bring items back to life, or find new uses for them, we see the tangible results of our actions and feel that we can make a difference."

Chornomorsk's underground gathering joins thousands of repair events planned worldwide for International Repair Day, from Egypt to India to the UK. But few carry such poignancy. For the Restart Project, a repair charity supporting the movement globally, the Chornomorsk festival represents something humbling: a community choosing to teach repair skills, share knowledge, and imagine a sustainable future—even from a shelter.
quick_facts: Chornomorsk Repair Festival moves to underground shelter on October 17
Previous venue destroyed by Russian missile strike on college building
International Repair Day events planned across Egypt, India, Ukraine, and UK
Festival includes bike, electronics, and clothing repair demonstrations
Organiser: 'We want young people to learn, create, and imagine their future'
